1bffdd959e.why: The pointing clause is gone. Two choices now concern the offspring, and only the unchilled one tests inheritance, so the T5 step (the new cold would explain the grain) is what decides the question. The facts check out: Lysenko soaked and chilled winter wheat; he claimed the change would be inherited; the vernalised state is reset in the embryo; Vavilov backed him at first.

82cc3fa48a.why: The lures are now count-shaped, and each is truly wrong: Kolmogorov found the scatter about as wide as chance predicts, and Stark and Seneta's corrected test still confirmed it (p about 0.09-0.11, not a too-close fit). 'bourgeois formalism' is gone. The card's unquoted 'claimed that mathematics had no place in biology' matches Wikipedia ('Lysenko boldly claimed that mathematics had no place in biology'). 'Whose work Lysenko backed' fits Stark and Seneta. The card's coin tosses are an analogy, not the dropped coin test.

4c4fbf023d.why: The key is supported. Wikipedia (Lysenkoism, citing Medvedev 1969, p. 125) has 'an order to destroy all stocks of Drosophila' among the directives of the months after the session, which fits 'In the months that followed'. The 2019 Genetics paper (Borinskaya, Ermolaev, Kolchinsky) names no organism; it says only that 'Mutant strains and various genetic preparations were also destroyed'. So it does not contradict the key, and asking which living thing the ORDER named keeps the mice and maize lures false. The Party politics are now setting only, and the card gives the harm in one clause. The 3,000 figure matches Wikipedia and Grokipedia; Borinskaya says 'several thousands'.

a6bd002c5c.why: The confounded lure is truly wrong: 'sown singly in a wetter land far away' changes water and place as well as crowding, so a good result there could not single out the crowding. Only the key changes the crowding alone, and the year and pine lures keep the nests. The stem credits the Ural die-off to Sukachev's record in Wikipedia's words ('Sukachev recorded that by September 1951, 100% of the trees planted using the nest method in the Ural territories had died', citing Brain 2010). 'followed the plantings' is gone, and the card now says critics blamed the crowding. Minor note: the card's 'by one estimate, only about a tenth' is unnamed in every source (Grokipedia, EBSCO), and others conflict (nearly half of the 1949 trees dead by 1951). It is hedged honestly. To name a source instead, delete that sentence.

cdf1d77ec1.why: The key no longer says 'genes', and 'of its day' fixes the size claim. The key fits Vavilov's aim (uniform crops lacked the diversity to withstand hardship; landraces and wild relatives hold traits breeders cross in). The arrest in 1940, death by starvation in Saratov in 1943 and the siege staff check out. Low note (older wording, not new): 'not only the best modern kinds' slightly undercuts the bigger-harvests lure; 'as well as the modern kinds' would remove it.

03fd123e17.why: Eugenics is now taught in the stem. The definition ('improve future generations by stopping people judged unfit from having children') is the negative eugenics the ERO pursued, and it stays true to Grokipedia's definition. The key and choices are unchanged and still sound: a pedigree cannot separate genes from a shared home. The card's Morgan and Jennings, the pellagra point and Harriman and Carnegie check out. Naming Morgan does not give away Q3's fruit flies.

362a80cd83.why: 'sworn expert judgement' no longer hints that he was absent. The card names Albert Priddy: he chose Buck's case to test the law (Encyclopedia Virginia, 'tabled all of the sterilization orders except for Buck's'), and Laughlin echoed his statements. The key fits Lombardo ('based on language given to him by doctors at the Virginia Colony'), and Priddy was the colony's superintendent and a doctor. Laughlin never met her (Wikipedia). The quote is exact.

6ec6415834.why: The coin is gone from the stem and card. The stem now gives only Estabrook's documented testimony (DNALC: 'the usual test for a baby of about six months old', which she failed; she was about seven months old, as the card says). The new lure 'A prize for arithmetic in her second year' is truly false: Gould's record has a D, then a C, then a failed term in maths, and no prize. The key holds (honour roll, April 1931, first grade). No choice says she was held back, which she was in 2A.

2242f92685.why: The padding is gone. The key matches the Avalon text word for word ('The voluntary consent of the human subject is absolutely essential'), and the lures are the Code's own 2nd, 3rd and 6th principles. The card does not give away the ninth-principle question.

cdbd26a180.why: LEAD FIX applied (2026-11-27): the re-checker's exact key wording. Re-checker's note: The stem matches the Code: Avalon (9) says the subject 'should be at liberty to bring the experiment to an end if he has reached the physical or mental state where continuation of the experiment seems to him to be impossible'. The key and the card are true, and all three lures are false. The remaining problem is a standout key, the same tell the judge flagged in the Bem question. All three lures share the frame 'He may stop [plus a condition]', and only the key is phrased differently ('He is free to bring the experiment to an end'). Added to the stem's 'seems to him', that lets a test-wise player pick it without knowing the Code. Exact fix: replace the key with 'He may stop, with no one's leave needed'. All four choices then open 'He may stop', and the card ('no doctor's leave, no reasons owed') still fits.
